title: Instrument Registry Rules and Additional Asset Fees (CalCare Tool Repair & Calibration Plan)
content:
The instruments covered by a CalCare Tool Repair & Calibration Plan are those on its instrument registry. Each registration records the customer's asset tag, the instrument class, the manufacturer and model as on the nameplate, the calibration interval in months and the registration date; a retirement records the asset tag, the reason and the retirement date.

## Registry rules

- Instruments are registered with their class and interval; an instrument registered without an interval gets the tier's default interval in months, and each next due date follows the tier's due date basis, with a recall reminder sent the tier's recall reminder days before it.
- Registered instruments above the tier's registry maximum, counted at the plan year start, carry the tier's additional asset fee each for the plan year; an instrument registered mid-year above the maximum carries the full annual fee.
- A retired instrument stays on the plan history and stops counting from the next plan year.

## How the registered count is taken

The count is the number of distinct asset tags whose most recent registry entry is a registration rather than a retirement. It is taken at the plan year start; for an instrument registered mid-year it is taken on its registration date.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

**Year-start count.** On a tier with a registry maximum of 50 and an additional asset fee of 6.00, a plan with 54 registered instruments at the plan year start has 4 instruments above the maximum, which carry 4 multiplied by 6.00, that is 24.00, for the plan year.

**Mid-year registration.** On the same tier, a plan already holding 50 registered instruments registers one more mid-year. The new instrument is above the maximum and carries the full annual fee of 6.00, not a part of it.

**Retirement.** An instrument retired during a plan year stays on the plan history. It was counted at that plan year's start and stops counting from the next plan year.

**Due date and recall.** An instrument with a 12-month interval last calibrated on 1 October is next due on 1 October of the following year; with a recall reminder of 30 days the reminder is sent on 1 September.

**No interval given.** An instrument registered without an interval takes the tier's default interval.
